sandhi.note: Final m before a consonant is written as anusvāra, twice.

morph.note: Past participle of √स्था with सम् + उप. With verbs of motion and standing the क्त participle is active and may take an object: तं मुनिं समुपस्थितौ ‘(they) approached the sage’. It serves as the finite verb.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) विप्र, ततः सहितौ तौ तं मुनिं समुपस्थितौ।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject (तौ, with सहितौ), object (तं मुनिम्), and the participle समुपस्थितौ as the verb; विप्र is a vocative aside. The two are named in 1.37.
mantras.lit: Then, O brahmin, those two together approached that sage —
mantras.tr: Then, O brahmin, the two went together to the sage:

comm.t: The king and the merchant go together to Medhas. The vocative विप्र is Mārkaṇḍeya’s address to his listener in the frame, the brahmin Krauṣṭuki — a reminder that the whole story is being told to him.

samasa.alt: Superlatives of selection are not compounded as genitives (‘best of kings’); the grammarians resolve them with the locative of the group.

samasa.literal: not going beyond what is proper
not going beyond what is fitting

morph.note: Nominative singular masculine (and feminine) of अदस् ‘that (yonder)’, the pronoun of distance.
Absolutive of √कृ (unprefixed, so -त्वा): ‘having made’. Its subject तौ is the subject of the main verb चक्रतुः in 1.38.
Accusative of संविद्, from सम् + √विद् ‘to know together’: agreement, mutual understanding; with कृ ‘to come to terms, exchange courtesies’.

mantras.anvaya: समाधिः नाम असौ वैश्यः सः पार्थिवसत्तमः च। तौ तु तेन यथान्यायं यथार्हं संविदं कृत्वा, (उपविष्टौ …)
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line names the two (in apposition to तौ of 1.36). The second line opens a new sentence with an absolutive clause; its main verb (चक्रतुः) is in 1.38.
mantras.lit: — that merchant named Samādhi and that best of kings. And the two, having made with him, as was proper and as was fitting, an exchange of greetings,
mantras.tr: the merchant Samādhi and the noble king. When they had greeted him with due courtesy, as was fitting,

comm.t: The two exiles are named side by side and come before the sage in due form. The courtesies are not skipped: the teaching that follows begins with the proper approach of the pupil.
A modern reading: the merchant’s name, Samādhi, is the word for meditative absorption. The text does not comment on it, but at its end (13.15ff) it is he who asks for knowledge rather than a kingdom.

sandhi.note: The visarga of काः becomes s before c, and the s becomes ś next to the palatal: काः + चित् → काश्चित्, whose t then becomes c before चक्रतुः.

samasa.sense: Samādhi and Suratha, named as a pair

morph.note: Perfect of √कृ, third person dual: reduplication च (k → c) + क्र + the dual ending -अतुः.
Past participle of उप + √विश् ‘to sit down’ (श् + त → ष्ट), active in sense: ‘having seated themselves’.
The indefinite pronoun: a form of किम् with the particle चित् (‘some’). It is one word and declines in its first part (कश्चित्, काश्चित्, केचित्).

mantras.anvaya_en: The main clause of the sentence begun in 1.37: subject वैश्यपार्थिवौ, participle उपविष्टौ, object कथाः with काश्चित्, verb चक्रतुः.
mantras.lit: — seated, the merchant and the king held some talks.
mantras.tr: the merchant and the king sat down and spoke with him a while.
mantras.tr_note: ‘with him’ is carried over from तेन in 1.37.

comm.t: The scene is set for the teaching: the two are seated before the sage and the conversation begins. The king’s question follows.

mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: Suratha now puts to the sage Medhas the question both exiles share (1.40–45).

sandhi.note: Final n before t becomes ṃs (anusvāra + s): भगवन् त्वाम् → भगवंस्त्वाम्. The m of त्वाम् joins the vowel of अहम्.
Final i before e becomes y; the m of प्रष्टुम् joins the following vowel.
Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

morph.note: Infinitive of √प्रच्छ्: the root-final छ् becomes ष् before त्, which becomes ट् (प्रच्छ् + तुम् → प्रष्टुम्).

Imperative ātmanepada of √वद्, a root normally parasmaipada. Pāṇini allows the ātmanepada of वद् in certain senses, among them speaking with knowledge or expertise; here it suits a request for instruction. It is also common in epic usage.
Vocative of भगवत् (‘possessed of fortune, revered’), the -vat stem: nominative भगवान्, vocative भगवन्.

mantras.anvaya: भगवन्, अहं त्वाम् एकं प्रष्टुम् इच्छामि; तत् वदस्व।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two clauses: the wish to ask (इच्छामि with the infinitive प्रष्टुम् and its two objects त्वाम्, एकम्), and the imperative वदस्व with तत्.
mantras.lit: Revered one, I wish to ask you one thing; tell (me) that.
mantras.tr: Revered sir, there is one thing I wish to ask you. Please explain it to me.

comm.t: The king formally asks to put a question. After the approach (1.36–38) comes the request, and then the question itself (1.41–45).

The shape is that of a classical teaching dialogue: a pupil who has come with due courtesy asks one question, and the teacher’s answer becomes the text. The rest of the Devī Māhātmya unfolds as Medhas’s answer.
